podcast.body: Released after a three-year break following "Blood and Chocolate," this album solidified Costello's reputation as an influential "artist's artist" among fellow singer-songwriters. It famously includes a collaboration with Paul McCartney, signifying his high regard within the music community. "From 1989 and a record called Spike, there's just on that features Paul McCartney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

podcast.body: This album was Costello's debut for Warner Bros. and featured the lead single "Veronica," co-written with Paul McCartney. The album marked a significant commercial breakthrough for Costello, producing his first and only US Top 20 pop hit with "Veronica," which climbed to number 19 on the Hot 100 after first topping the Modern Rock Chart. "Released in the winter of 1989 as the lead single from Costello's new Warner Bros. album, Spike, Veronica first rose to number 1 on the Modern Rock Chart for 2 weeks."
